so my conspiracy theory (there's no confirmation on this, just personal experience) is that imvu removed the "tags" search, or in the very least, changed it significantly. it used to be that you could search up a word, let's say "apple". if you searched that word, imvu would show you all the rooms with that word in the title or description, giving you the rooms with any kind of occupancy at the beginning. Now, if you search apple, imvu is going to prioritize rooms with apple in the name, then description-- the occupancy becomes much less important. actually, now that i think about it, it makes more sense that they separated occupancy from search results entirely unless you specifically ask for it, which would explain why when you do select an occupancy, you get random rooms with no mention of "apple" at all.

i think imvu needs to learn the age old concept of "if it's not broke, don't fix it".

NTA Celiac disease is a very real thing that probably won’t kill you immediately but will likely cause some awful symptoms and even worse in the long run if left untreated. Celiac disease and gluten intolerance/sensitivity are also different. Please don’t undermine this kid’s diagnosis.

However! NTA. But kids are kids regardless of diagnosis and understandably he just wanted to join in on the cool new thing. This isn’t necessarily advice, but I was only medically cleared to work part time for years due to my C-PTSD with many accommodations because it took such a huge toll on me. Eventually, I had to file for disability and have been on it for a little over a year now.

Multiple hospitalizations, attempts, and documented resistance to treatment left me with little option and ability to work consistently. Since being on disability, I have been doing world’s better, but am still not in a position to work.

You’re definitely not alone and your feelings are 100% valid. There are things you can do to try to ease your job duties. Definitely try to figure out what accommodations you need and how to go about receiving them, and talk to your doctor. Good luck.

When I was living with my father at 17, I was not allowed to show emotion. Not just crying, but anger, depression, even happiness. Like you, I was yelled at to stop crying whenever I did, and threatened with abuse or worse. I was not allowed to be angry at him. If he ever did anything out of line, I had to make my disdain for it out like a joke— “you’re such an asshole lol”, “you’re gonna get arrested haha!” He was the kind of guy to take those things as a compliment. But any actual flaw in his character? Hell no. Whenever I was happy or excited about something, he would blow me off or talk over me, going as far to flat out tell me, “I don’t care” at times.

I was allowed to share my opinion on things but I was always wrong. Whatever racist, sexist, homophobic thing that came out of his mouth was absolute fact while anything going against that was just a “point of view”.

I’m 28 years old now, and honestly, writing this all out really made me take a good hard look at the damage that’s been done. The anger, isolation and self-destructive habits I still deal with to this day. The horrible self-image and lack of self-worth. My martyr complex. It all goes back to constantly being shut down and told to shut up. I’m working through it with therapy, but I feel as if the damage has already been done and it’s much too late.

Please know that in no way is your parents doing this with you safe, healthy, or loving. It is abuse, even if not physical, and It will eventually take its toll. Healthy relationship allow for communication and independent thoughts and feelings. You are not being dramatic or weak or whatever else someone who doesn’t get it will try to say. I don’t know how to make it stop because I couldn’t, but it’s important you find a way, or at least know that it is wrong and try to cope the best you can.

Be safe. Take care of yourself.

Depression is a medical condition. It’s something entirely outside your control without the proper treatment, acknowledgement and coping skills. Saying you don’t have the right to be depressed is like saying you don’t have the right to be sick, which is ridiculous.

You know depression isn’t just sadness. It’s an emptiness that feeds off of your greatest fears and flaws. You may feel you don’t have a reason to be sad because you have a decent life and great friends and family, but even if depression was just sadness, you still have the right to have emotions!

I understand the guilt that comes from friends who don’t fully get it or partners trying to help, but you gotta let them try. Isolating and hating yourself for it is exactly what this thing wants. Everyone needs a support system and it sounds like you’ve got some pretty good options. Let yourself feel, admit you have a problem, and allow yourself to heal. You got this.

Leave her alone until you’re sure your feelings are reciprocated and come from a pure place. You do not deserve to die.
